key_insight: OctoSense introduces a rich open-source multimodal sensor platform and dataset that helps robots learn robust perception from synchronized real-world data, even when some sensors are degraded. The key idea is to use self-supervised learning across many sensor types to improve robot understanding without requiring expensive manual labels.
problem_solved: Robots often struggle to perceive reliably when conditions change, sensors fail, or individual modalities become noisy or unavailable. This paper addresses the lack of large, synchronized, multimodal datasets for training perception models that can handle real-world degradation.
method: Builds the OctoSense platform with stereo RGB, event cameras, LiDAR, thermal imaging, IMU, RTK-GPS, and proprioceptive signals from cars and quadruped robots.
Collects 59 hours of time-synchronized driving data across diverse environments, times of day, and degraded-sensor scenarios.
Uses self-supervised multimodal learning to extract useful representations from the aligned sensor streams without relying on dense human annotations.
impact: This work gives AI and robotics researchers a practical foundation for training perception systems that are more robust to missing or degraded sensors. It can accelerate development of multimodal, label-efficient robot perception models for real-world deployment.

paper_title: OctoSense: Self-Supervised Learning for Multimodal Robot Perception
paper_authors: Anthony Bisulco, Jeremy Wang, Kostas Daniilidis, Randall Balestriero, Pratik Chaudhari
